content.thinking:
I'll write the whole file carefully in one pass, checking what needs importing—the builder creator, rng, svg texture helpers, and paint utilities—before structuring the default export function.

Now I'm planning the bookshelf design itself: a 1.4m wide, 0.4m deep, 2.2m tall dark wood unit with an arched top and three shelves holding books, scrolls, orbs on stands, and candles, all built from boxes and cylinders with modest color variety. I'm laying out coordinates for the side panels, back panel, and shelf boards before placing the decorative items.

Adding gold trim sweep and wood grain textures...

Now I'm designing a book helper for the shelf: a cover box sized to width/height/depth with a painted finish, plus a slightly inset cream page block, oriented so the spine faces outward along the front.

With pages visible from the top, each book comes to about 9 parts, so 40 books lands around 360 parts, comfortably under my 1000-part budget. For leaning books, I'm planning a helper function that tilts a book about the z-axis by rotating each sub-part's local offset around a pivot, so I can position tilted spines resting against their neighbors without needing actual joints.

Now I'm working out the row-generation logic: a function that places books along a shelf, advancing x by each book's width plus a small gap, using randomized heights, widths, and depths for variety, with the tilt helper handling center-position offsets so the books look naturally placed.

I'm settling on a z-center of 0.0 with depth 0.28 so book fronts sit at 0.14, leaving room on the shelf front edge for other decor. Then I'm picking a palette of eight cel-shaded book colors—deep red, royal blue, emerald, purple, teal, burgundy, ochre, and cream-blue—to randomize across the rows.

For spine decoration I'm planning gold flat bands, a small cream plate box, and tiny rune-glyph decals on select spines, rendering simple SVG rune paths onto planes facing +z, while skipping the decal or adjusting rotation for tilted books.

Designing three rune symbols: a circle-and-cross glyph, a star polygon, and a crescent, all in gold strokes on a small viewBox. Now I'm laying out the shelf compartments across four rows and mapping out where book stacks and objects will sit within each.

Continuing shelf 2 with books and a bookend on the left, a glowing orb on a gold stand centered, and scrolls with candles on the right; shelf 3 gets a row of books, a pair of small orbs, a candelabra, and a hanging star mobile. For the crown, I'm placing an orb at the very top center above the pediment.

Topping the whole structure with a glowing star finial, then adding floor items around the base: a stack of tomes with a dripping candle on one side and a leaning scroll bundle on the other, kept roughly symmetric around center. I'm setting up helper functions for placing parts as boxes with position, color, and rotation.

Now I'm designing the candle itself — cream-colored wax cylinder with drip details, a tiny dark wick, and a glowing flame made from stretched spheres in warm yellow-orange tones, sitting on a small gold lathe-turned dish.

For the orb, I'm considering how to make a glass sphere read well visually — maybe layering an outer translucent colored sphere with a lighter glowing core, or instead wrapping a single sphere with a painted nebula-style texture (radial gradient, stars, swirls) to fake depth and glow without needing true transparency.

Still designing scroll helper...

I'm sinking the scroll bottoms into the pot with slight tilt variation. For extra charm, I'm thinking about adding hanging details like small gold star charms or tassels dangling from the shelf edges, and maybe little ribbon bookmarks hanging out of a few books for a cute touch.

Actually, I'll place gold tassels hanging from the front edge of each shelf board, a few per board, dangling into the compartments below. I'm also adding a thin gold trim strip along the front of each shelf board for a finished look.

Now I'm thinking about a decorative painted band for the shelf fronts, using a small SVG texture with a repeating diamond motif in gold on a dark background, kept efficient as a single shared texture. I'm also considering adding filigree detailing to the front faces of the side support posts to match.

Adding vine pattern SVG...

I'm also planning the posts' material with wood grain shading, plus a bottom plinth box with a dark stained finish and a stepped moulding strip for detail. For the back panel, I'm considering a deep indigo color with a starry texture to add visual depth.

Adjusting the z-positions so the back panel sits just behind the shelf boards without visible z-fighting, tweaking board depth slightly so edges line up cleanly around z=-0.17 to -0.175.

I'm checking compartment free heights against book sizes to confirm clearance, then deciding against using a point light since the glowing orbs handle illumination on their own. Now I'm working out the color and material setup for the books, using a seeded random generator to pick spine colors and deciding whether to add subtle texture variation like stripes or mottled patterns to some spines for visual variety.

Writing book geometry function...

Adding the gold rune plane...

I'm estimating part counts per book (around 9 each, roughly 360 total plus extras) to stay under the 1000-triangle budget, with simple boxes keeping triangle counts low. For the flat horizontal stack, I'm figuring out orientation — deciding whether to rotate the book 90 degrees about z so the spine faces outward while lying flat.

Good, the lying-flat spine texture reads rotated 90 degrees, nicely realistic. Now I'm designing an orb-and-stand helper: a lathe profile for a small pedestal with a cupped top, sized relative to the orb radius, with the sphere nestled into the cup at a computed height above the stand's base.

I'm also adding decorative touches—a tilted gold equatorial ring around the orb and a few tiny glowing sphere "stars" floating nearby for a halo effect—while sketching the sphere's texture as a gradient-and-circles nebula pattern to simulate an equirectangular surface.

Building the candle geometry... wax cylinder body with drip details, a small meltpool disc on top, thin wick cylinder, and a glowing flame ellipsoid for the light source.

Now I'm designing the gold dish beneath the candle as a lathed profile, plus a candelabra function with a turned stem base and swept arms holding three candles.

Now I'm designing the pot on the floor as a lathed vase with a closed solid profile, then adding a paint callback to give it a deep teal ceramic color with gold bands at specific height bands.

Adding scroll helper logic...

Now I'm planning scroll piles for the shelves, using a vector helper to position rolled scrolls lying horizontally with slightly sloppy rotations, stacking a few on shelf 2 and shelf 3. I'm settling on concrete shelf-top Y coordinates for the layout.

For the base shelf, I'm working out a flat-lying book stack on the left with varying lengths and thicknesses, computing the stack height and checking that a small orb placed on top clears the shelf above.

Centering a pile of three scrolls lying sideways in the middle, stacking two side by side and one on top, offset slightly from center. On the right I'm laying out upright books in a row, with the last one leaning against the post at a negative tilt, building a function to generate each row's positions.

Still working out lean logic...

So for a positive tilt, the rightmost extent of the rotated book works out to w/2·cos + h/2·sin, meaning the uprights should fill up to x1 minus twice that extent, leaving the leaning book's center positioned at x1 minus the extent so its corner just touches the boundary.

Now I'm implementing both lean directions, filling the uprights row by placing book centers incrementally with small gaps, and varying book heights with a minimum and occasional tall ones. I'm working out the x-positions for each shelf's row and pile layouts, checking that the spans don't overlap and gaps look right between flat stacks and piles.

For shelf1 I'm laying out the left row, a cyan orb centerpiece with its halo height checked against the ceiling, and a candelabra on the right with flame height confirmed to fit under the shelf above. I'm adding a small stack of flat books near the right edge to fill remaining space, working out their exact x-span.

For shelf2 I'm starting a scroll pile arrangement on the left, spacing a pyramid of six scrolls by length and radius to fit the shelf's available width.

Adding a tilted row of books, an amber orb resting on a flat stacked tome base at x=0.42, and a lone candle on a dish nearby at x=0.58, checking that spacing stays clear of the stack and post. Moving on to plan shelf 3's bounds next.

Now I'm placing floor items: a stack of four graduated books with a candle on top at the left, and on the right a pot with a small cyan-green orb nearby, checking their footprints against the shelf plinth width for clearance.

A horizontal scroll lies on the floor at the front left, keeping the overall scroll count modest. Up top I'm working out the crown/pediment geometry above the shelf, positioning a cap board centered around y=2.08 spanning the compartment width and depth.

Now I'm shaping the crown outline wider than the posts below it, with a scalloped silhouette rising to a sharp peak in the middle and tapering concave curves on each side. Once the shape is set, I'll paint it with a wood-grain cel shader and a gold border trim.

Then I sweep that outline upward at a slight offset to give the crown real depth, keeping it centered on the posts beneath. I'm adding a small decorative moon-and-stars decal on the front face as a gold accent, and considering a finial orb on top to cap it off.

Placing the glowing finial orb at the crown's peak with a lathe-formed cup beneath it, bringing the total height to around 2.55 units. I'm also adding gold spike finials at both ends of the crown and gold box caps along the side posts to reinforce the structure visually.

Now I'm working out the plinth and post proportions — a wide gold base box with decorative studs along the front, posts spanning roughly 0.64 to 0.72 in x, and a moulding step box to add detail between the plinth and the posts above it.

Adding gold decor planes for each board front, positioning them at the right heights and depths, then working out the cap board's thicker front plane. For the texture trim, I'm sketching an SVG band with a dark background and a repeating chain of gold diamonds along a center line.

Now I'm moving to the post vine texture, setting up its viewBox and plane proportions so the aspect ratio stays consistent for the tall post geometry.

Writing wavy vine path...

Now I'm sizing the fence posts and back texture plane, checking that post geometry at x=±0.68 with 1.9m height matches the viewBox scale of 10x380 units, confirming the unit conversion of 0.005m per unit so the board fronts don't collide with the post planes.

For the starry background texture, I'm generating an SVG with a dark indigo gradient, scattering random gold and pale stars as circles, and connecting some into constellation polylines, keeping stroke widths thick enough to stay visible at scale. Then I'm adding hanging tassels from the board bottoms and cap, working out the cord rod positions for each board and the center cap point.

Now I'm building each tassel's geometry—a thin red cord, a small gold knob sphere, and a flared cone body with the apex pointing up so it narrows toward the knob and widens at the bottom—checking that they hang low enough without colliding with the front-facing books or other objects.

I'm also considering adding tiny glowing motes around each orb for extra sparkle, then tallying up my flat color palette to make sure I stay within the 64-color budget—gold, dark gold, dark wood, indigo, cream, parchment, red ribbon, wax tones, and flame colors.

Now I'm defining the wood grain paints for different box orientations, using darker grain for the plinth and crown pieces, making sure the cel grain function works correctly in model space with the unrotated geometry.

Writing builder code...

Still defining geometry helpers...

Building out the spine panels and page block, then realizing I need a back cover board too — adjusting the pages' depth and z-offset so they sit properly between front and back covers without clipping through the spine.

Making pages slightly shorter than the boards so they stay recessed under the covers, then positioning gold decorative bands near the spine's top and bottom with a third one added conditionally for wider books, keeping their depth just proud of the spine face.

Now I'm adding a rune emblem plate positioned above center on the spine front, sized relative to the book width and using a texture cycled from the rune set with some rotation, plus a pair of thin cream accent lines beneath it to suggest a title plate. Starting to set up the row generation function with randomized book dimensions...

Still writing row logic...

Checking the tilt extent matches, swapping the infinite loop style, and aligning book depths so all backs stay flush while fronts vary for a natural shelf look.

Now I'm writing a lathe-based function for a decorative orb shape with a gold rounded profile, defined by a set of points for its silhouette.

Adding gold claws and tiny motes around the rim, checking that the claws reach up along the sphere's curvature without clipping into it.

Still writing candle geometry...

Shaping the gold candelabra stem with a lathed profile, then sweeping curved arm shapes outward on each side.

I'll smooth the arms using a catmull-rom path helper for natural curves, then place the center and side candles with heights computed to stay within the shelf clearance. After that I need to add the scroll function, floor pots, and a motes function for ambient particles.

Now I'm defining glowMotes to scatter small glowing spheres, then assembling everything to return the root node. For the orb textures, I'm setting up color palettes for cyan, violet, and amber variants, and writing an SVG generator with swirling stroke paths for each orb's surface pattern.

I'm working out the texture mapping conventions to place a bright highlight ellipse at the correct equirectangular coordinates so it appears on the orb's front-facing surface, accounting for rotation offsets, plus scattering star circles at fixed positions.

Now I'm sketching simple gold rune decals as small SVGs — a crescent shape, a five-point star polygon, and a rune combining a circle with a cross — to use as decorative moon crown elements.

Using a mask to carve the crescent shape with gold fill, then adding star dots nearby. I'm skipping ornate extras like bookends and hinges to keep things simple, and now working out how to lay flat tilted books on the floor stack with proper position math for the 90-degree rotation case.

Adding slight random jitter to the stacked books' position and tilt angle so they look naturally placed rather than perfectly aligned...

Writing scroll and ribbon helper functions...

Adding scroll materials and frame geometry...

Topping it with a small lathed cup and a glowing cyan orb finial, using an orb helper function to stack sphere and stand geometry. Computing the total height comes to roughly 2.6m, which feels like a reasonably grand shelf scale.

Adding gold crown spikes at the sides and a base sphere, plus a gold trim sweep embedded slightly into the crown face. Finally I'm double-checking that all imports — THREE, createBuilder, rng, catmull, grain, mottle, paint, svg — are actually used in the build.

Now I'm working out the tassel positions hanging below the cap, writing a helper function that creates a cord rod at each tassel point with a fixed radius and red color.

Placing the floor-end scrolls and then working out the pot scrolls: positioning several scrolls around the pot with slight tilt directions and offsets so their bottom ends stay within the pot's radius while fanning outward naturally.
